findings.issue: Queue-writing public APIs do not state exact logical Device/Queue/destination provenance. New observation scopes context.device, but SDK queue write failures route through queue's sink. Externally constructible context/buffer handles do not prove their pairing.
findings.remedy: Document write/write_at/from_upload preconditions: destination belongs to context.device and context.queue is paired with that same logical Device. Canonical from_parts/context docs may own the pair contract with API links. State no runtime branding/provenance check is performed.
findings.constructor_disposition: Buffer::new only creates on context.device; do not invent a queue requirement for this device-only operation. Document allocation origin/validation-policy meaning and that creation Ok does not certify arbitrary context.queue pairing.
findings.acceptance: Public docs accurately distinguish caller preconditions, observed Validation and borrowed/browser device-handled paths; no runtime query/brand requirement added.

findings.issue: Rationale says Texture3d presentation renders into this sRGB format. Current tracked source has no context.blitter consumer; Texture2d's actual blit constructs its own Blitter. The named behavior cannot be established from current code.
findings.remedy: Remove or qualify the unsupported named consumer rationale. A public optional Blitter configured for sRGB does not prove a current Texture3d presentation path.
findings.acceptance: Comment describes actual supported behavior/policy without inventing an unchanged consumer.

findings.issue: Borrowed bytes are said to be retained through queue submission. BufferUpload is consumed by write_buffer; SDK copies host data into staging during that call and permits discarding it before later Queue::submit.
findings.remedy: Say native element bytes are borrowed through the write call. Distinguish that CPU copy from the queued GPU transfer starting at later submission.
findings.acceptance: Both owning type prose and directly affected buffer guide state the actual lifetime; no host source retention or completion guarantee invented.

verified_no_additional_owned_wording_fin: Buffer read documents same logical device/paired queue, external unmapped/exclusive mapping ownership, producing-submit handling, logical zero/host-layout/padding and native/browser progress.
Typed destination allocation occurs before mapped view. AnyBitPattern, aligned destination and initialize-before-set_len safety explanation match code. try_reserve preserves actual allocation source.

MappingRequest owns callback/cancel cleanup; no SDK scope guard is stored across await. Successful views are dropped before release. Drop's native Validation-only cleanup exception is documented even for borrowed contexts and does not poll or promise an operation verdict.
Native failed map wrapper requested state and native Idle NotMapped cause justify cleanup-only scope. Other classes/later health/universal runtime success are not promised.
observe_validation closure/scope synchronous and thread-local; no poll or completion wait. Read completion separately calls explicit native Wait; browser awaits callback.
Logical zero returns empty after host-layout admission; physical padding excluded. Native capability/alignment remains native admission, not silently padded.
Source-preserving BufferReadError, GenerateErrorGpu(anyhow), Readback/Staging causes and MetalDeviceError reflect actual source carriers rather than declaring irrecoverable device loss.
Armor module no exactly-once/arbitrary resource concurrency promise; Metal constructor docs say six handles reused. Armour scratch uses byte min4; Metal scratch counts native words with min1.
Staging session identity, exact-count prefix, ZST/foreign/short failure, status one-word admission and missing-byte rejection agree with source; no synthesized missing payload.

Initialization preserves actual native adapter/device/surface errors and original opaque JS Canvas cause. JsValue is not a standard Error source; no fabricated source claimed. No atomic-Wasm compile assurance.
Current inline test bodies/oracles and existing BufferUpload doctest remain unchanged by source diff; no new cases/helpers/assertions introduced by this repair.
